title: Turn Structure & Signals
summary: Decouple the table UI from the rules with Godot signals: announce turn changes, card plays, and penalty updates without hard references between nodes.

lessons.title: Signals for Turn Events
lessons.bodyMarkdown:
# Signals

A **signal** is a message a node can emit; other nodes connect callbacks to react. Signals implement the **observer pattern** — the rules engine shouts "turn changed" without knowing who is listening.

```gdscript
class_name TurnManager
extends Node

signal turn_changed(player_index: int)
signal card_played(player_index: int, card: CardData)
signal penalty_updated(new_total: int)

var current_player: int = 0
var penalty_stack: int = 0

func advance_turn() -> void:
    current_player = (current_player + 1) % 4
    turn_changed.emit(current_player)

func play_card(card: CardData) -> void:
    card_played.emit(current_player, card)
    if card.is_penalty():
        penalty_stack += card.penalty_value()  # 2, 3, or 5 (Joker)
        penalty_updated.emit(penalty_stack)
```

`card.penalty_value()` returns the Kadi penalty a card demands — a 2 is worth 2, a 3 worth 3, and a Joker worth 5 — never the raw rank, or a Joker (rank 15) would wrongly force the next player to pick up 15 cards.

Declare signals with `signal name(args)`. Emit them with `.emit(...)`. Connect from a listener using `turn_manager.turn_changed.connect(_on_turn_changed)` in `_ready()`.

Godot 4 lets you pass typed arguments on signals, so the editor and autocomplete know what each event carries. Connect signals in code (not just the editor) so connections survive renames.

> [!WHY]
> Signals break the dependency cycle. The TurnManager does not import the UI; the UI does not import the TurnManager. The manager emits; whoever cares connects. You can swap the human HUD for an AI-driven debug overlay without touching a line of the rules engine. This is the single biggest decoupling in the project — without it every node would `get_node("../UI/Label")` and the scene graph would be uneditable.

Use signals for one-to-many notifications; use direct function calls for one-to-one commands.

quizQuestions.prompt: How do you emit a signal named `turn_changed` with one integer argument?
quizQuestions.explanation: In Godot 4, signals are first-class objects — call `.emit(...)` on them with the arguments.

quizQuestions.prompt: Why prefer signals over direct method calls between nodes?
choices: They decouple emitter from listener — the emitter does not know who is listening, so you can swap UIs without touching the rules
quizQuestions.explanation: Signals implement the observer pattern: the emitter stays ignorant of subscribers, enabling clean swaps and one-to-many notifications.

lessons.title: Building the Turn Manager
lessons.bodyMarkdown:
# Building the Turn Manager

Kadi's turns are trickier than "next player, please". Kickback Kings reverse the direction of play, Jump Jacks skip players, and the table can seat 2 to 5 people. All of that lives in one dedicated script: the **TurnManager**, registered as an Autoload so every scene sees the same turn state.

Two variables carry the whole system: `current_player_index`, and `direction`, which is `1` for clockwise and `-1` for counter-clockwise. A Kickback simply flips the sign: `direction = -direction`.

```gdscript
extends Node

signal turn_changed(player_index: int)

var current_player_index: int = 0
var direction: int = 1
var player_count: int = 4

func advance_turn() -> void:
    current_player_index = (current_player_index + direction + player_count) % player_count
    turn_changed.emit(current_player_index)
```

The advance formula deserves a close read: `(current + direction + player_count) % player_count`. The modulo `%` wraps the index around the table — player 3 plus 1 becomes player 0 in a four-player game. But GDScript's `%` can return a negative result for negative operands, so when `direction` is `-1` and the index is `0`, plain `(0 - 1) % 4` would give `-1` — an invalid seat. Adding `player_count` before the modulo keeps the left side non-negative, so the wrap is always into `0..player_count - 1`.

Every time the turn moves, the manager emits `turn_changed`. The HUD highlights the active player's hand, an AI player wakes up, a timer restarts — all as listeners, none hard-wired into the manager.

> [!WHY]
> Centralising turn order in one Autoload means Kickback and Jump cards are one-liners: `direction = -direction` for a King, one extra `advance_turn()` call for a Jack. If each scene tracked its own idea of whose turn it was, a single reversal would desynchronise the table — the HUD showing player 2 while the rules engine waits on player 3. One writer, many listeners: that is the TurnManager contract.

With turns wrapping correctly in both directions, the special cards of Phase 5 become small tweaks instead of rewrites.

codeSnippets.code:
extends Node

signal turn_changed(player_index: int)

var current_player_index: int = 0
var direction: int = 1  # 1 = clockwise, -1 = counter-clockwise
var player_count: int = 4

func advance_turn() -> void:
    current_player_index = (current_player_index + direction + player_count) % player_count
    turn_changed.emit(current_player_index)

func reverse_direction() -> void:
    direction = -direction
codeSnippets.caption: The TurnManager Autoload: wraparound advancing plus a Kickback-ready reversal.

practicePrompt.instructions: Add a method `skip_player()` to the TurnManager that advances the turn twice (the Jump Card effect: the next player is skipped), reusing advance_turn().
practicePrompt.hint: Call advance_turn() twice — the second call lands on the player after the skipped one.

quizQuestions.prompt: Why does advance_turn add `player_count` before taking the modulo: `(current + direction + player_count) % player_count`?
choices: It keeps the result non-negative when direction is -1, since GDScript's % can return negative values
player_count must appear in every formula
quizQuestions.explanation: With direction -1 and index 0, `(0 - 1) % 4` would yield -1 — an invalid seat. Adding player_count first guarantees the wrap lands in 0..player_count-1.

quizQuestions.prompt: A Kickback (King) is played. What single change does the TurnManager need?
quizQuestions.explanation: Reversal is just negating direction; the existing advance formula then walks the table the other way automatically.
